subject: microbiology
title: Hepatitis A, Hepatitis B Markers, HBsAg, HBeAg and Anti-HBc IgM

steps.tx: **Hepatitis A virus** is a non-enveloped picornavirus spread faecal-orally through contaminated water, food and close contact. It causes acute hepatitis only, never chronic carriage. Children often have silent infection, while adults develop fever, nausea, jaundice and marked transaminase elevation. Anti-HAV IgM marks acute infection; total anti-HAV or IgG indicates past infection or vaccination. Effective vaccines exist.
steps.say: HAV is acute and faecal-oral; IgM makes the current diagnosis.

left.title: HAV course
points: Incubation about two to six weeks
Faecal shedding greatest before jaundice
Fulminant failure is rare
No chronic hepatitis or carrier state

right.title: Serology
points: Anti HAV IgM positive in acute disease
Anti HAV IgG persists for protection
Vaccination produces IgG without IgM pattern
Household contacts may need vaccine or immunoglobulin

steps.tx: **Hepatitis B virus** is an enveloped partially double-stranded DNA hepadnavirus with reverse transcription. **HBsAg** is surface antigen and the screening marker of current infection. Anti-HBs is protective antibody after recovery or vaccination. Anti-HBc indicates natural exposure at some time; its IgM form supports acute infection, while total anti-HBc persists after resolved disease.
steps.say: HBsAg says infected now; anti-HBc says naturally exposed sometime.

left.title: HBsAg present
points: Current HBV infection
Acute versus chronic decided by duration and IgM
HBV DNA quantifies replication
Test HBeAg and anti HBe for phase

right.title: HBsAg absent
points: Anti HBs alone suggests vaccine immunity
Anti HBc plus anti HBs suggests resolved natural infection
Isolated anti HBc needs careful interpretation
Occult infection may require HBV DNA in special settings

steps.tx: **HBeAg** marks high viral replication and infectivity in many HBV phases, while anti-HBe seroconversion often accompanies lower replication. HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis can still have high DNA from precore or basal core promoter variants. HBV DNA is therefore the direct replication measure; HBeAg status alone must never be used to declare disease inactive without DNA and ALT.
steps.say: HBeAg is a replication clue, but HBV DNA gives the actual load.

left.title: HBeAg positive
points: Usually high HBV DNA
High infectivity in blood exposure
May be immune tolerant or immune active by ALT
Mother to child transmission risk rises

right.title: Anti HBe positive
points: Can be inactive carriage with low DNA
Can be HBeAg negative active hepatitis
Serial ALT and DNA separate the two
Fibrosis assessment influences treatment

steps.tx: **Anti-HBc IgM** is the best serologic marker of acute hepatitis B when HBsAg may already be disappearing in the window period. In chronic infection flare, anti-HBc IgM can also be detectable at lower levels, so clinical and quantitative context matters. Isolated anti-HBc can reflect resolved infection with waned anti-HBs, false positivity, occult HBV or the acute window.
steps.say: Anti-HBc IgM rescues acute HBV diagnosis when HBsAg has just vanished.

left.title: Acute HBV pattern
points: HBsAg positive or recently cleared
Anti HBc IgM strongly positive
ALT often very high
Anti HBs appears during recovery

right.title: Chronic HBV pattern
points: HBsAg persists beyond six months
Total anti HBc positive
Anti HBc IgM usually negative or low
Phase defined by DNA, ALT and HBeAg

steps.tx: The infectious **Dane particle** is the complete 42-nanometre HBV virion, while infected serum contains far more noninfectious spherical and tubular HBsAg particles. That excess explains why HBsAg tests are sensitive screening tools. HBV DNA integrated into hepatocyte genomes and covalently closed circular DNA in nuclei make sterilising cure difficult even when plasma DNA becomes undetectable on therapy.
steps.say: Most HBsAg particles are empty decoys around a minority of infectious Dane particles.

left.title: Particles
points: Dane particle contains DNA and core
Spheres and filaments are HBsAg only
HBcAg is not ordinarily free in serum
HBeAg is a secreted processed core product

right.title: Persistence
points: cccDNA persists in hepatocyte nucleus
Integrated HBV DNA can produce HBsAg
Functional cure means sustained HBsAg loss
Immunosuppression can reactivate occult infection

steps.tx: A safe hepatitis screen records **HBsAg, anti-HBs and anti-HBc** where status matters because one marker alone leaves dangerous ambiguity, particularly before immunosuppression. Vaccinated responders show isolated anti-HBs. Resolved infection carries reactivation risk with potent B-cell depletion even if HBsAg is negative, so anti-HBc positivity changes prophylaxis decisions.
steps.say: Three HBV markers prevent the commonest interpretation and reactivation errors.
